presentation.label: SAMPLE LOCKS
presentation.summary: Lock Part sample choices into pattern trigs, or clear SAMPLE locks.
presentation.overview: Two explicit native SAMPLE-lock actions in Part Edit. Lock preserves existing SAMPLE locks by default. Clear removes every SAMPLE lock on selected tracks. Playback keeps its current state; successful settings are remembered while the module stays loaded.
highlights: All eight tracks appear; only Flex and Static tracks are selectable.
Select all eligible tracks or a subset.
Keep existing sample locks by default.
Clear removes every SAMPLE lock on selected tracks, including manual locks.
Recall separate Lock/Clear selections and Lock replacement policy during the current module session.
usage: MKII: FUNC + PART, then choose either sample-lock action.
Level 2: arrows navigate eligible tracks; A selects all, B selects the highlighted track. Turn clockwise ON, counterclockwise OFF.
C sets Replace existing for Lock; Clear always includes every SAMPLE lock.
YES opens level 3 with per-track change counts. NO returns to level 2; NO in level 2 closes.

limitations: Experimental: tested on one MKII over USB; no MKI, no audio checks on this base.
Under a high-load development run, SAMPLE fields on one pattern changed without explanation; the cause is unknown.
On a unit that had run a long session, the menu rows once did not appear until a power cycle; cause not found.
Clear removes all SAMPLE locks on selected tracks, including manual locks.
Lock preserves all existing SAMPLE locks by default, including those written by a previous Lock action.
No ownership storage, origin tracking or custom lifecycle event is used.
First-beta scope is USB-only through the Modwerk base; card firmware is unsupported. Contributed-machine combinations remain unqualified.

resources.recorded: Author's MKII, 8 Nov 2026; emulator 8 Nov 2026; exact package extent

storage.label: Storage
storage.conditions: Exact extent in the Octatrack base's shared 768 KiB runtime pool: one active copy per module ID. Replacement can retain both old and new extents; 21,664 bytes assumes both are this candidate. Reclamation depends on reachability. Excludes complete shared sys-task stack demand. See TESTING.md.

processing.label: CPU / DSP load
processing.display: Dearest press 333,805 instructions in the emulator
processing.conditions: ot_emu, exact package 3e13c46f on base 9b3ba417: one Clear on 512 SAMPLE fields, entry to return of module_key, stock callees and interrupts included. A one-shot edit on the UI task; nothing in the audio frame or on the DSP. On the MKII a separate probe measured the Clear commit body at 8.36 ms with USB recording. See evidence/performance.json and TESTING.md.

impact.conditions: One USB-installed MKII 1.40C instance per module ID. Normal dispatch includes module_tick at 60/s and module_draw on each composed frame: while CLOSED, key checks code/consumed bits then normally returns, encoder exits at its phase check, tick writes api->value, and draw exits. In an open Part Edit popup, ticks check popup/source, draws paint the menu/overlay each composed frame, and key/encoder events update bounded state and request redraw. Also includes one maximum explicit Lock or Clear at a time over up to eight selected Flex/Static tracks × 64 steps (512 SAMPLE fields), stopped or playing; live/sampler recording refuses. Playback is stock; no DSP/frame callback is added. Candidate occupies the shared pool; 21,664 bytes assumes an equally sized old extent. Upload stage, base ledgers and task stack are shared; other combinations, MKI, card and high-load extremes are outside scope. Complete memory/stack qualification remains open.

cpu.rationale: Low remains a relative source estimate for this mixed workload, not an exclusively one-shot or zero-idle-cost rating. With the popup closed, key/encoder hooks do brief input/phase checks, tick makes one api->value update at 60/s, and draw exits each composed frame. While open, ticks check popup/source state and each composed frame paints a fixed-size menu/track overlay; key/encoder paths update bounded UI state. These hooks persist but add no audio-frame processing. For maximum 8×64 Clear, a source-mapped, path-conditional envelope counts 5,502,242 candidate ColdFire instructions in the transaction core but excludes the ui.c wrapper/state-capture/redraw work, stock callees, interrupts and scheduler; it is not a full callback bound, cycle count, latency or hardware measurement. Apply Scene's Low tier covers a measured one-press path up to 11.1 million emulator instructions with nothing between presses, so it is only a coarse ordinal reference and does not include these persistent hooks. See ui.c, TESTING.md and the instruction-envelope report.

dsp.rationale: The package adds no DSP program or audio-frame callback. Lock/Clear writes ordinary SAMPLE fields that the instrument's existing playback path consumes. Minimal describes the absent added DSP path, not zero whole-instrument DSP load; playback continuity and full-load qualification remain separate.

memory.rationale: One active copy occupies an exact 10,832-byte extent in the shared runtime pool: 8,748 initialized bytes, 1,328 BSS bytes, 528-byte runtime header and 216 site-record bytes plus alignment. Apply Scene's 2,062-byte code/state is a minimal-tier reference; Temp Save's 42,892-byte buffer is moderate. The 10,048-byte package occupies existing shared upload staging, not another module allocation. The complete shared-task/interrupt stack remains unresolved, so this is not a total-memory qualification; the 21,664-byte overlap assumes two equal candidate extents.

tests.summary: On the author's MKII (OS 1.40C, public beta base 9b3ba417) over USB, 8 Nov 2026, exact package 3e13c46f: with 20 kept published modules plus Sample Locks, FUNC + PART showed both actions; Lock on two patterns wrote SAMPLE locks and kept a manual SAMPLE lock and a non-SAMPLE lock; native save and reload kept both; Keep of the 21-module set survived a physical power cycle with both patterns' locks; Clear on one pattern removed its SAMPLE locks, kept the non-SAMPLE lock and stayed clear after save and reload. Earlier the same day the menu rows did not appear on a long-running unit until a power cycle (cause not found). 3 Nov: Replace OFF kept an existing lock and filled an empty field; Clear kept non-SAMPLE locks. Emulator: dearest press (Clear on 512 fields) 333,805 instructions; 40 presses while playing, no hang. Not run: MKI, audio, live-recording refusal on this base, a static cycle or stack bound. Known issue: one unexplained SAMPLE change in a high-load development run.

conditions.parameterExtremes: The dearest input: CLEAR SAMPLE LOCKS confirmed on 8 tracks x 64 steps, 512 SAMPLE fields. Five cases measured (2, 64 and three 512-field fixtures); the next dearest was 326,556.
conditions.parameterModulation: Not applicable: no continuous parameters. Encoders and arrows change bounded UI state; each change costs one redraw.
conditions.modeSwitching: Lock and Clear, Replace existing on and off, stopped and playing; 20 rounds of Lock then Clear on 512 fields while playing, with STOP and a Part change between (40 events, no hang).
conditions.maxLoad: One instance per module ID. The event is one module_key call on the UI task, not an interrupt. Budget: the key-press template's 26,600,000 cycles (100 ms at 266 MHz), owner-waived static bound for this version.
conditions.inputConditions: ot_emu, executed instructions from entry to return of module_key, stock callees and interrupts included, DSP running; exact package 3e13c46f on base 9b3ba417. Instructions, not cycles: the figure is a count of executed instructions; even at ten cycles each it stays under 13 % of the budget. Not measured on hardware.

regions.name: ColdFire code and initialized data (package image)
State (bss): menu, selections and edit plan
Runtime module header, three site records and alignment in the base's pool

memory.conditions: From the exact package 3e13c46f (10,048 bytes, 167 relocations) and the base's loader layout: one 10,832-byte extent in the shared 768 KiB runtime pool; during a replacement the old and new extents can both be held (21,664 bytes for two copies of this package). No DSP memory, no heap, no battery storage, no card files. Stack: the key path's source-derived subtotal is 916 bytes on the shared sys task, excluding interrupts; not measured on hardware.

hardware.summary: The author's MKII, OS 1.40C, flashed public Modwerk beta base 9b3ba417, driven over USB by Claude Code with whole-set offers. 8 Nov 2026, exact package 3e13c46f beside the 20 published modules the unit keeps (set 42fcda34): FUNC + PART on a Flex track's SRC page showed LOCK SAMPLES TO PATTERN and CLEAR SAMPLE LOCKS; Lock on two patterns wrote SAMPLE locks and kept a manual SAMPLE lock and a non-SAMPLE lock; native save and reload kept both; Keep of the 21-module set (self-test 21 intact, 6 DSP effects ran, 0 failed) then a physical power cycle restored all 21 records and both patterns' locks; Clear on one pattern removed its SAMPLE locks, kept the non-SAMPLE lock, and stayed clear after native save and reload while the other pattern kept its locks. 3 Nov 2026, same package in a RAM trial: Replace OFF kept an existing manual SAMPLE lock and filled an empty field; Clear removed selected SAMPLE locks and kept a non-SAMPLE lock; rollback restored the set.
limitations: Panel results are the author's reports; the USB readings (set identity, self-test, status word) were observed by the session.

Earlier on 8 Nov, on a unit that had run a long session, FUNC + PART showed only the stock rows in three trials until a power cycle, while Beat Slicer's tick signature stayed in the shared status word after its removal; cause not found, not reproduced in the emulator.
In one high-load development run, SAMPLE fields on one pattern changed without explanation; cause unknown.
Not run on this base: audio checks, live or sampler recording refusal, Apply while playing on the unit, maximum-size edits on the unit.
Cost measured in the emulator in instructions, not cycles; no static cycle bound or measured stack depth (owner-waived for this version).

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Create a disposable pattern with sample trigs and an existing SAMPLE lock.
Open Lock, select a track and leave Replace existing OFF. Confirm: empty SAMPLE fields on sample trigs receive the Part assignment; existing locks remain unchanged.
Open Clear and select tracks. Review **INCLUDES MANUAL LOCKS** and the counts. Confirm to remove every selected SAMPLE lock. Other parameter locks remain.
Use ordinary Save Project to save the pattern. Nothing saves implicitly.

steps: FUNC + PART opens level 1; select an action with YES.
Level 2 always shows T1-4 left and T5-8 right. Arrows skip greyed-out non-Flex/Static tracks.
Turn A clockwise to select all eligible tracks or counterclockwise to clear selection. B sets the highlighted track in the same way.
For Lock, C sets Replace existing; OFF preserves every existing SAMPLE lock. Clear always includes all SAMPLE locks.
YES opens level 3. Review per-track change counts; YES applies and closes on success, NO returns to level 2. Errors remain visible.
NO in level 2 closes the popup. Apply keeps playback as it was; active live or sampler recording refuses the edit.
Successful operations remember each action’s tracks and cursor, plus Lock replacement policy. Cancelling keeps the previous settings. Module reload or power cycling resets them.
